correctness.rationale: At exponent one the local ratio is 1+1/p; at exponent at least two the denominator contains both p and p^a, so the ratio is below one. Truncated valuations partition the corresponding prime-power residue classes, including one zero class per prime. The Chinese remainder theorem gives the finite convolution. An independent integer replay by trial-division prime generation, exact binary search for bins, and dictionary convolution verified 1000*count>216*modulus over the 96 primes; the diagnostic prefix proportion is 0.2161377019267721. On this periodic set the prefix log is at most −41 log(4001/4000)≤−41/4001<−1/100. For the tail, expand the exponential as a product of nonnegative indicators of squarefree divisors, each with frequency at most 1/d. This bounds the finite-sample exponential moment without an independence assumption. Enlarging the prime sum to all integers and integrating the decreasing summand gives F(1400/503). A separate rational bound summing through order 20 and bounding term ratios by 1/7 proves F<7; a finite lower Taylor sum proves e^7>1000. The frequency with S≥1/100 is therefore uniformly less than 1/1000. The reverse strict set has liminf at least dens(G)−1/1000>0.215, which by disjointness gives the claimed ceiling (even for the forward upper asymptotic density). Trudgian supplies existence of the natural density. The original script was inspected, not executed; replay with python3 /workspace/replays/5.py.
